items: frequently tested: Are the recommendations of the Finance Commission binding on the Union Government? (Answer: No, they are advisory only).
Statement verification: The government can reject recommendations but is constitutionally required to present an explanatory memorandum detailing reasons to Parliament.
Crucial distinction: Differentiate between the recommendatory nature of constitutional advisory bodies and the binding decisions of judicial or quasi-judicial tribunals.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Recommendations made by constitutional and statutory bodies (such as the Finance Commission, UPSC, and NHRC) are advisory in nature and not legally binding on the government.
There is no constitutional provision that mandates the executive to accept or implement these recommendations.
If the government decides to reject or modify any recommendation, it must lay an Explanatory Memorandum before Parliament stating the reasons for non-acceptance.
Established democratic conventions dictate that recommendations concerning financial devolution and meritocratic appointments are usually accepted unless there are compelling reasons.
